name: Designer Monographs
tagline: In-depth studies of the designers behind the objects.
seoDescription: Monographs on great industrial and furniture designers: Dieter Rams, Charles & Ray Eames, Achille Castiglioni, Jasper Morrison and Enzo Mari.
intro: A good monograph does more than catalogue a designer’s output. It shows how one person’s constraints, clients and obsessions turned into a recognisable body of work, which is exactly what a student or young designer needs to learn from.
These books cover four very different attitudes to industrial and furniture design: rigorous reduction, playful experimentation, quiet everyday restraint and outright rebellion against the market.

name: Materials & Manufacturing
tagline: How things are chosen, shaped and made.
seoTitle: Materials & Manufacturing Books for Designers | Acceso
seoDescription: The best books on materials selection and manufacturing processes for industrial, product and furniture designers.
intro: Most design problems are solved or ruined at the point where a material meets a process. Knowing what injection moulding, die casting or steam-bending can and cannot do lets you design things that can actually be made at a sensible price.
This collection mixes engineering-grade references with visual guides written for designers, so you can start with process overviews and go deeper when a project demands it.

name: History & Theory
tagline: The ideas, arguments and movements behind modern design.
seoDescription: Essential design history and theory books: Papanek, Pevsner, Sudjic and Braungart on objects, responsibility and sustainability.
intro: Design history is not trivia. The debates about ornament, industrial production, social responsibility and sustainability are the same ones designers still argue about today, just with different materials.
These four books give you a spine for that conversation: how modern design saw itself, what it got wrong, what objects say about us, and how products could be rethought as part of material cycles.

name: Product Design
tagline: Process, usability, sketching and the business of making products.
seoTitle: Product Design Books: Essential Reading | Acceso
seoDescription: Essential product and industrial design books on usability, development process, sketching and design reference.
intro: Product design sits between people, engineering and the market. The books here cover each corner: how people understand objects, how teams develop them, how to put ideas on paper, and how the field has looked over a century.
They are practical rather than theoretical, and most are the kind of book that is still being handed from one designer to the next.

name: Furniture Design
tagline: Timber, joinery, production and the culture of sitting.
seoTitle: Furniture Design Books: Essential Reading | Acceso
seoDescription: Furniture design books for makers and designers: development and manufacturing, understanding wood, and the cultural history of the chair.
intro: Furniture is one of the few design disciplines where craft, industry and the human body all meet in the same object. Good furniture design depends on understanding all three.
This collection includes a practical introduction to furniture development, the definitive technical book on wood, and a cultural history of the chair.

name: Graphic Design
tagline: Type, grids and visual thinking for product-minded designers.
seoDescription: Graphic design and typography books for industrial and product designers: type, grid systems and visual thinking.
intro: Industrial designers spend more time than they expect on presentations, packaging, labels and interfaces. A working grasp of typography and layout makes every other part of the job look better.
These three books are short, visual and practical, covering type, grids and a broader way of seeing the everyday.
